boards.title: Motion spec — timing, easing, rules
boards.name: MotionSpec
boards.text:
Motion
Play curves
ENTER
cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1)
Things arriving: sheets, pages, covers landing.
EXIT
cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15)
Things leaving: dismissed sheets, old chapter.
STANDARD
cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
Moves within the screen: tabs, toggles, tiles.
SPRING
cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1)
Small pops: press release, badge, red dot.
DURATIONS
100 ms
Press feedback (scale 0.97)
200 ms
Toggles, chips, tab pill
300 ms
Sheets, nav, tile expand
400 ms
Stack shuffle, page turn
450 ms
Shared cover → novel / reader
600 ms
Theme switch reveal
COLOUR VS DOT
Colour — smooth. Background colours morph between books; covers fly as shared elements; springs on sheets.
DOT — STEPPED. SAME TIMINGS, BUT FILLS AND FADES ADVANCE DOT BY DOT (STEPS(8)); NO COLOUR MORPH; RED DOT PULSES ONCE ON ARRIVAL.
RULES
Every animation is interruptible; tapping again reverses it.
Never animate text while someone is reading it.
Reduce-motion: all transitions become 150 ms fades.
Nothing longer than 600 ms; content is usable at 60% through.

Chapter 412 · The Index of Ash

The Head Archivist kept no candles in her office. She said it was a matter of principle, but Ilse had come to suspect it was simply fear: a room without flame was a room in which nothing could be forgotten by accident.

“You read it,” the old woman said, without looking up. It was not a question.

“I read the first page.” Ilse set the ledger on the desk between them. “Then I couldn’t stop. Every name has a date beside it, and none of the dates have happened yet.”

For a long moment the only sound was the scratch of a pen. Then the Head Archivist capped it, folded her hands, and finally met Ilse’s eyes.

There was something in them Ilse had never seen there before, and it took her a breath to name it. Relief.

“Then it has chosen,” the Head Archivist said. “Good. I was beginning to worry it would choose no one at all.”

“Chosen me for what?”

The old woman rose, crossed to the shelf behind her, and drew out a second ledger — identical in every way but one. Its pages were blank, and its spine was warm to the touch, as though it had only just stopped burning.

The ledger lay open on the reading desk, its pages the colour of weak tea. Ilse had tried three times to burn it. Three times the flame had curled away from the paper like a cat refusing water.

“Names do not burn,” the Head Archivist had told her once, “unless someone has stopped saying them.”

She said them now, under her breath, one after another — Corvin Hale, Ada Merrow, Tobiah of the Lower Stacks — and with every name the lamp above her steadied, as if listening.
